title: Anomaly detection without labels in the engine: a review list, measured on planted anomalies, with its limits
request: The missing family as a kind with its own machine: detectors, evaluation without labels (planted anomalies, stability, a review budget), partial labels joining the rare-event kind, and a review loop where confirmed cases become labels. The owner's morning on a replica with no label must end with a ranked review list, its evaluation on planted anomalies and the honest limits; with a label file it moves to the rare-event kind.
spec: A portable library of detectors, planting and splitting; a kind whose machine runs the five stages with no target; Home builds it; a route takes confirmed alerts into labels.
plan: Survey the kind machinery and the no-label pieces.
Write the library: split by day, features with entity behaviour, detectors, planted shapes, the choice on validation, the review.
Write the kind and its machine; let a solution have no target for this kind only.
Build it from Home; add the review loop; accept it on the replica.

decisions.decision: A detector is chosen on anomalies planted in a validation period, never on the rows to review.
decisions.why: With no label, planted shapes are the only truth, and the rows to review play the holdout's part.

decisions.decision: Its measure is called what it is: recall on planted generic shapes, never a precision.
decisions.why: Nobody has labelled the real anomalies; a number that sounded like precision would overclaim.

decisions.decision: A solution may have no target only for a kind that says it needs none.
decisions.why: Every other kind learns from an outcome, and a missing one must still be refused.

decisions.decision: Confirmed alerts become partial labels, their selection by the detector written in their provenance.
decisions.why: A rare-event model trained on them partly measures the detector again; the person must see that.

findings.defect: A continuous fare was dropped as an identifier.
findings.scenario: The fare, unique on every row, was left out of the detectors.
findings.cause: Any column unique on every row was taken for an id.
findings.fix: Only unique integer columns are row numbers.

findings.defect: A second round of review was refused.
findings.scenario: After the first confirmation the project had no anomaly solution left.
findings.fix: The review keeps its own record (key column, rounds) on the project.

findings.defect: The rows to review were scored without history.
findings.scenario: Their entity counts and usual places covered one or two days against the training rows' week; the list leaned on that difference.
findings.cause: Behaviour features were computed inside each frame transformed.
findings.fix: Scored rows are transformed with the earlier rows as their history, keeping theirs.

findings.defect: A refused confirmation still wrote its keys.
findings.scenario: Typos stayed in the case file and spoiled later rounds.
findings.cause: The file was written before the label check.
findings.fix: Keys the table does not hold refuse the round before anything is written; each round attaches its own file.

findings.defect: The first confirmation erased the review list.
findings.scenario: Confirming two of fifty alerts deleted the record of the other alerts.
findings.fix: Each round's review list is kept on the project.

findings.defect: After confirmation the project became binary unless its pack was imbalanced.
findings.scenario: An acceptance-built project with no pack resolved to binary.
findings.fix: The suggestion names the rare-event kind.

findings.defect: The anomaly solution was written at build without the graph check.
findings.scenario: No check, log, memory or audit for the built solution.
findings.fix: It goes through the same block as the wizard's solution.

findings.defect: The key was a payment reference, and a check counted a set of keys.
findings.scenario: On seed 3 an order listed twice failed the list-size check; Home keyed rows by terminal_ref.
findings.cause: Order ids repeat and the key had to be unique on every row.
findings.fix: The list's length is checked; Home prefers a nearly unique id column; ids shown without .0.

findings.defect: The limits said the shapes were the analysis' own.
findings.scenario: The planted shapes are a fixed generic set.
findings.cause: The wording promised more than the code does.
findings.fix: The limit names the three generic shapes.

findings.defect: A table with nothing numeric crashed the models stage.
findings.scenario: No numeric column and no entity raised inside the planting.
findings.fix: Refused at the leakage stage and in the library.

findings.defect: Labels from the review loop did not say how they were picked.
findings.scenario: A rare-event model on them partly re-measures the detector.
findings.fix: The provenance names the detector's selection; rejected alerts are kept as reviewed.

findings.defect: The identifier rule read the rows to review.
findings.scenario: Uniqueness was measured over every row.
findings.cause: The whole frame was read in the leakage stage.

findings.defect: No labels with an outcome was accepted.
findings.scenario: A binary solution with labels none was treated as complete.
findings.cause: The new value was not checked against the kind.
findings.fix: Refused for every kind that learns from an outcome.

findings.defect: The review-loop test passed on files and failed on PostgreSQL.
findings.scenario: The milestone gate's PostgreSQL run answered 404 for a project the test had just built.
findings.cause: The test built its project in a file store beside the server, which on PostgreSQL never reads that folder.
findings.fix: The acceptance builder takes an open store; the test builds in the server's own store.

measurements.name: the owner's morning with no label, four seeds
measurements.gate: a review list at least ten times above the fake trips' rate, the rows to review read once, the limits stated
measurements.result: 7 to 13 fake trips in lists of 36 or 37 rows, against rates of 0.0070 to 0.0108; 0 self-deliveries listed
measurements.against_gate: 7 of 37 against a rate of 0.0070 at worst: well above ten times the rate

outcome: Anomaly detection without labels runs in the engine as its own kind: a review list measured on planted anomalies with its limits, built from Home, and a review loop that turns confirmed alerts into rare-event labels.
lessons: Features that count over history must be computed with the same history for every row they compare.
Validate a person's keys before writing anything a later round reads.
Name a measure for what it measures: recall on planted shapes is not precision.
risks: No page shows the review list yet.
